title: The Predator Principle — The Cancer of Evolution
description:
Predation, generalised into the organising principle of a system, is malignant. That is a diagnosis, not an insult, and this project states it plainly.

The lion is bound. It kills inside a web of feedback that answers back: prey grow scarce, populations fall, the pattern corrects itself. What we describe is what happens when that binding is cut — when extraction keeps its gains, sends its costs elsewhere, disables the correction, forces escalation, and consumes the ground it stands on. Nuclear arsenals are that pattern raised to the level of the species. The sixth mass extinction is that pattern running now. Neither is a test awaiting results.

Life did not begin by eating, and for most of its history it did not eat at all — it lived on chemistry and light. Its greatest leaps in complexity ran through cooperation and the containment of conflict at the level below: the complex cell is two bacteria that stopped devouring each other. Devouring is one late possibility among several, not the essence of life. That is why the diagnosis is not a verdict. A pattern that was adopted can be revised, and the same evolution that ran blind has now produced an agent that can recognise it and change it.

Every claim in this corpus carries its evidence status — E for empirical evidence, I for interpretation, P for a proposition still to be tested — together with its boundary. This release contains the essay corpus, the claim and source registers as machine-readable JSON, the published dispatches, and the automation that keeps them in sync.
